[LTIM.6.5] **A component of a `Time` is a function of the instant and a
zone.** A component read on the result of `.utc` or `.local(tz)` ([LTIM.6.1])
is that component of the instant in the zone: UTC for `.utc`, and for
`.local(tz)` the zone `tz` names, resolved per [LTIM.10.7]. It is an `Int` in [LTIM.6.3]'s range. Each component
is its own builtin, taking the instant and the zone name — `FN_HOUR`,
`FN_MINUTE`, `FN_SECOND`, `FN_DAY`, `FN_MONTH`, `FN_YEAR` and `FN_DAY_OF_WEEK`
in `proto/builtin_fn.proto` — and the compiler **must** lower a component read
to it.

**The zone `UTC` is offset 0 and consults no fact** ([LTIM.10.8]), as `.utc`
itself does not, so a component read in UTC works on an engine that holds no
`TimeZoneOffset` fact. Every other zone is resolved through its facts, with
[LTIM.10.5.3]'s failures.
